body: airBaltic plans to cut around 100 pilots and around 200 cabin crew members in its latest savings drive, the airline has confirmed to AeroTime. The numbers are not yet final and may change once staff assessments are complete. The Latvian Aviation Union (LAU) said on October 29 that around 300 airBaltic employees will start learning whether they will keep their jobs from October 31.

The announcement follows airBaltic's October 5 announcement that 500 to 700 employees could lose their jobs in a wider workforce adjustment aimed at securing the airline's future. The October 29 report sets out the crew-specific detail and timetable within that wider adjustment, rather than an additional headcount on top of it. LAU has called for the crew assessment to be paused and for talks on the selection criteria and method, saying the criteria have not been provided to the union in writing and that individual notices should be held until the criteria and method have been jointly reviewed.

airBaltic said the cuts are linked to the flight volume and route network planned for next year. Pilot reductions will affect all three of its bases, while the airline said Riga has more staff than needed and that, where possible, staff will be offered positions at the other two bases, which are short-staffed. On selection, airBaltic said the criteria were decided after several rounds of consultation with unions, as a compromise using the company's existing assessment system for pilots and cabin crew, taking into account seniority and professional qualifications among other job-related factors. The airline's all-Airbus A220-300 fleet is set to fall from 54 aircraft to 36 by the end of 2026, before gradually recovering to around 40 by about 2031.
en.summary: airBaltic plans to cut around 100 pilots and 200 cabin crew, with individual notices starting October 31; the airline says the numbers are not yet final, and the move is the crew detail of its wider October 5 workforce adjustment.
en.title: airBaltic plans to cut around 100 pilots and 200 cabin crew, with notices from October 31

body: airBaltic計畫在最新撙節措施中裁減約100名機師與約200名空服員，航空公司已向AeroTime證實此事；數字尚未定案，員工評估完成後仍可能變動。拉脫維亞航空工會於10月29日表示，約300名airBaltic員工將自10月31日起陸續得知自己是否保住工作。
本次公布接續airBaltic於10月5日的宣布，當時稱在為確保航空公司未來而進行的較廣泛人力調整中，500至700名員工可能失去工作；10月29日的報導是該調整中的機組人員細節與時程，而非在上述人數之外另加的人數。工會要求暫停機組評估並展開會談，稱遴選標準未以書面提供給工會，個別通知應在標準與方法經共同檢視前暫緩。

airBaltic表示，裁員與明年計畫的飛行量與航線網絡有關；機師人數減少將影響其全部三個基地，里加基地人力多於所需，在可能的情況下，員工將獲安排至另外兩個缺人的基地。遴選方面，航空公司表示標準是在與工會進行多輪諮商後決定，折衷採用公司既有的機師與空服員評估制度，考量年資與專業資格等與職務相關因素。airBaltic全AirbusA220-300機隊將由54架減至2026年底的36架，之後逐步回復至2031年左右的約40架。
zh.summary: airBaltic計畫裁減約100名機師與200名空服員，個別通知自10月31日起開始；航空公司表示數字尚未定案，本次是10月5日較廣泛人力調整中的機組人員細節。
zh.title: airBaltic擬裁約100名機師與200名空服員　個別通知自10月31日起開始
